correctness.rationale: In the defining lattice, q(v)=x²+t x S+2S²−3T, d=(v,h)=2x+tS, and the exact identity d²=4q(v)+(t²−8)S²+12T gives for roots d²=(t²−8)S²+12T−4. S=0 is ruled out by squares modulo 12; |S|≥2 yields d²≥4t²−20>t²; |S|=1 yields d²≥t² with equality precisely T=1. This proves the six positive shortest roots for every t≡3 mod12. Root effectivity plus minimality makes each an irreducible smooth rational curve. The primitive ample square-two class defines a finite smooth-sextic double cover: anisotropy excludes elliptic exceptions and h⊥ contains no roots. The deck involution acts v↦(v,h)h−v; it pairs the six roots into three plane images; the six generated classes span <e1,e2,e3,th> of exact index t. Standard facts invoked: K3 lattice realization, Saint-Donat degree-two projective model, RR and adjunction, rational invariant cohomology for a finite quotient. The finite verifier did not substitute for these proofs.

value.rationale: The polarization degree of the first smooth rational curve is a natural enumerative invariant of a genus-two K3 model. The result gives its exact unbounded value t and complete six-curve minimizer census, three distinguished rational sextic contact curves, their intersection configuration, and an increasing saturation defect t in Picard rank four. It connects the recently introduced hyperbolic-automorphism lattice family to classical smooth plane sextic geometry; the genus-two model alone would be routine, but the exact shortest-curve and index data are not.
